title: Ikhfa and the noon sakinah check: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Qadr, Al-'Alaq 1 to 12 and the noon sakinah rules
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 17 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ikhfa and the noon sakinah check rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 17. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

blocks.title: Sort into: Izhar / Idgham / Iqlab / Ikhfa
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Izhar, Idgham, Iqlab, Ikhfa.
blocks.answer: Izhar: مِنْ عَلَقٍ; عَنْهُ. Idgham: مِّن مَّسَدٍ; وَيْلٌۭ لِّكُلِّ. Iqlab: مِنۢ بَعْدِ; لَيُنۢبَذَنَّ. Ikhfa: مِّن كُلِّ; أَنزَلْنَٰهُ

keywords.def: hiding the noon with a light humming sound
a humming sound from the nose, held for two counts
a noon with a sukoon on it: نْ
a double vowel at the end of a word that sounds like an extra noon

questions.q: Read «أَنزَلْنَٰهُ» (97:1): find the noon and name the rule.
questions.a: The noon before zay (ز) is ikhfa: read an-zalnaahu with a light two-count hum.

questions.q: Noon sakinah check (pupil PDF): for ten words from Al-Qadr, Al-'Alaq and Al-Masad, write the rule. Today's rota group recites 96:1 to 12 to the teacher in turn.
questions.a: 1 مِنْ عَلَقٍ izhar; 2 أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ikhfa; 3 مِّن كُلِّ ikhfa; 4 خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ idgham with ghunnah; 5 مِّنْ أَلْفِ izhar; 6 أَن رَّءَاهُ idgham without ghunnah; 7 إِن كَانَ ikhfa; 8 مِّن مَّسَدٍ idgham with ghunnah; 9 لَهَبٍۢ وَتَبَّ idgham with ghunnah; 10 عَبْدًا إِذَا izhar.

questions.q: Extend: write the fifteen ikhfa letters from memory.
questions.a: ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك

questions.q: Stretch: explain to the class the difference between ikhfa and idgham with ghunnah.
questions.a: Idgham: the noon disappears into the next letter (shaddah). Ikhfa: the noon is hidden but not merged; no shaddah.

questions.q: «مِّن كُلِّ» (97:4): the next letter is kaaf (ك). Which rule?
questions.a: A) Ikhfa. Kaaf is one of the fifteen ikhfa letters. It is not a throat letter (izhar) or in يَرْمَلُونَ (idgham).

questions.q: Think again: Is hiding always bad? When the Qur'an 'hides' a noon, why might that make the recitation more beautiful?
questions.a: Ikhfa is a gentle, half-hidden noon with a hum: smoother than a clear noon, lighter than full merging.
